comment.narrative: Around 62 of respondents in Papua stated that the government has an important role in conflict resolution and around 61 respondents argued that church has an important role as well. The traditional customary or adat is considered as protector ofcommunity members.

title.narrative: Number of advocacy initiatives targeting policy makers

description.narrative: Number of advocacy initiatives (in the form of Action Plan/Policy Brief in 9 districts) targeting local government at district & regency level to agree on a peace agreement/policy.

comment.narrative: Respondents mentioned a limited number of advocacy initiatives addressing conflicts targeted by policy makers. In the conflict analysis workshop there was a suggestion to develop a policy for pinang and sagu sellers as the sellers often compete with each other with the OAP continuously asking the government for regulations. Advocacy for alcohol abuse was another initiative suggested as a policy already exists however the enforcement of the policy is low and needs to be increased.Several land conflicts were mentioned by respondents in the qualitative study highlighting the importance of community or customary leaders helping address land related conflicts.In the qualitative study the advocacy initiatives mentioned include independent advocacy efforts through writing and publications and activities led by several communitybased organizations such as Papua Cinta Damai and Lembaga Bantuan Hukum Papuan which provide assistance to resolve conflicts.

title.narrative: Extent to which stakeholders endorse the peace agreement

description.narrative: Extent to which stakeholders endorse the peace agreement

comment.narrative: This study found that several stakeholders assist in endorsing the peace agreement. The qualitative study found that most respondents identified the church and religious leaders as endorsers and promoters of peace. Further it found thatcustomary governments through community leaders often promote peace and tolerance through mediation when conflicts happen incommunities. Commitment for peace as found in this study is about consistency in spreading moral messages about peace through socialization and that the continuing presence of leaders has impacted resolving conflict.There were several peace agreements mentioned by respondents such as the implementation of fines as a form of retributive justice in conflict resolution and peace treaties which involve the signatures from all parties. Fines are mandatory to aid stakeholders engaged in conflict resolution processes. Fines can include money and livestock with money often used as a method to pay those engaged to help resolve conflict.
